headline: Forecasters held to a dry midweek, then a stormy Pacific pattern grew wetter, windier, and coastal-flood prone.
summary:
From the start, forecasters saw a quiet, foggy, dry stretch under a ridge of high pressure (a dome of settled air) on Thursday and Friday, and that call never wavered. What changed was the outlook beyond it. On Tuesday, Nov 17, the jet stream (the fast band of high-altitude wind) was expected to dip over the Pacific and aim stronger storms at us early the following week. Later in the week the weekend looked weak, with only light lowland rain and a little mountain snow. By Saturday, Nov 21, a cold upper-level low was expected to stall offshore, then get pulled into a broad dip in the winds over the northeast Pacific around Monday, opening the door to a string of storms.

The storm week also came into sharper focus. Coastal flooding at high tide, and strong winds and high seas on the coast, went from a passing mention to the main concern. Early on, the worry was Tuesday. By Sunday, Nov 22, the first flooding risk was moved up to Monday morning on the Grays Harbor coast, and wind and flood warnings replaced watches. By Monday, Nov 23, forecasters expected repeated rounds of rain, mountain snow, and southeast winds through Thursday, with the worst flood risk on the Olympic Peninsula and the coast. They were fairly confident about Wednesday's coastal flooding but less sure about the strength of the Wednesday-into-Thursday system and tide timing on the Strait and Sound. A break is expected Friday, with winds returning next weekend.

turning_points.what: Forecasters added a wetter, windier pattern for early next week, as the jet stream was expected to steer stronger storms toward us.
Confidence grew in strong coastal winds peaking Tuesday, and a light Saturday evening rain and snow forecast was added.
The offshore low's stall and its pull into a broad trough became clear, and coastal flooding became a growing concern.
The main flooding risk moved up to Monday morning's high tide, and a coastal flood warning and wind warnings were issued.
